_README: Copy this file, put YOUR prices in it, and pass it as --rates to
scripts/cost.py. PyHunt ships no rate card and never will: a price
depends on the contract you are billed under and on a date, neither of
which is visible from inside a scan. Every number below is a PLACEHOLDER
and is deliberately zero, so an unedited copy produces a total of 0.00
rather than a plausible-looking figure nobody checked.
'source' and 'as_of' are required. cost.py refuses a table without them,
because a dollar figure with no provenance is exactly the unfalsifiable
claim this tool exists to avoid — it just happens to be about money.
Keys under per_million_tokens match a model id exactly, or by longest
prefix: 'claude-opus-5' matches 'claude-opus-5-20260101'. A model with no
matching key contributes nothing and is named in cost.json's
unpriced_models, which makes the total a stated floor rather than a
The four rates are priced differently on every card that distinguishes
them at all. Cache reads dominate token COUNT on a long run — 98.8% of
traffic on the recorded scan — while costing the least per token, which
is why cost.py never sums them into a single headline.
source: REPLACE ME — where these prices came from
